chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Prayer is performed upon the deceased at any hour, for it is not a prayer of bowing and prostration; rather, prayer is disliked at the rising of the sun and at its setting, which are the times of humbless, bowing, and prostration, because the sun sets between the two horns of Satan and rises between the two horns of Satan.

key_terms.بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ: Between the two horns of Satan

ai.seo_question: Can funeral prayer be performed at any time of day?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that Salat al-Janazah is exempt from the specific times of makrooh (dislike) associated with the sun's rising and setting, as those prohibitions are tied to the ruku' and sujud of regular prayers. The hadith distinguishes the funeral prayer as a distinct act of worship lacking these specific postures, thereby allowing it to be performed at any hour. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the 'shaitan's horns' metaphor for sun times applies primarily to the five daily prayers rather than the funeral rite.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You can pray Salaat upon the deceased during every time. But rather, it is not a Salaat with a bowing or a prostration, and rather the Salaat is disliked during the emergence of the sun and during its setting, wherein is the humbleness and the bowings and the prostrations, because the setting is between the two horns of Satanla and the emergence is between the two horns of Satanla’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Afi af-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd af-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Musfim who has said the foiiowing: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

You can perform Salah (prayer) for a deceased anytime; it is not a Salah (prayer) with Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sujud (prostrations). Only on sunset and sunrise performing Salah (prayer) in which there is humbleness, Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sujud (prostrations) it is not desirable, because it sets and rises between the two Qarn (horns) of Satan.’” (Another meaning of the word ‘Qarn’ is a century)
